## Rationale

- **HG-SSH-001**: Direct root login over SSH gives attackers a single, well-known account to target and removes the audit trail of which person used administrative rights. Knowledge base: `knowledge/ssh-root-login.md`.
- **HG-SSH-002**: Password logins can be guessed or brute-forced from the network. Key-based authentication removes that whole class of attack. Knowledge base: `knowledge/ssh-password-authentication.md`.
- **HG-SSH-003**: If empty passwords are accepted, any account without a password can be entered remotely with no secret at all. Knowledge base: `knowledge/ssh-empty-passwords.md`.
- **HG-FW-001**: Without a host firewall every listening service is reachable from the network, including ones that were only meant for local use. Knowledge base: `knowledge/host-firewall.md`.
- **HG-NET-001**: Every service listening on a network interface is attack surface. Services that only local programs use should listen on loopback. Knowledge base: `knowledge/listening-services.md`.
- **HG-FS-001**: /etc/shadow holds password hashes. If other users can read it, they can crack the hashes offline; if they can write it, they can set any password. Knowledge base: `knowledge/shadow-permissions.md`.
- **HG-FS-002**: These files define every account and group. If a non-root user can modify them, they can create a root-equivalent account or join privileged groups. Knowledge base: `knowledge/passwd-group-permissions.md`.
- **HG-FS-003**: Files under /etc configure system services. A world-writable one lets any local user change how a privileged service behaves. Knowledge base: `knowledge/world-writable-etc.md`.
- **HG-ACC-001**: Any account with UID 0 is root, whatever its name. An extra one is a classic backdoor and is easy to miss in an account list. Knowledge base: `knowledge/uid-zero-accounts.md`.
- **HG-ACC-002**: Passwordless sudo turns any compromise of that user's session into full root access, with no second factor of the user's password. Knowledge base: `knowledge/sudo-nopasswd.md`.
- **HG-UPD-001**: Most real-world compromises use known, already-patched flaws. Applying security updates automatically closes that window without relying on memory. Knowledge base: `knowledge/automatic-updates.md`.
- **HG-KRN-001**: Address space layout randomization makes memory-corruption exploits unreliable, because attackers cannot predict where code and data live. Knowledge base: `knowledge/aslr.md`.
